How to turn an image into a coaster 3MF for Bambu Studio

Start with a PNG or JPG and turn it into a coaster with a solid base and separate color parts. The 3MF keeps the parts together so you can check the filament assignments in Bambu Studio before you print.

Open the Coaster Maker

1. Choose artwork that traces cleanly

Use a logo, illustration, or icon with a clear outline and a few solid colors. A transparent PNG is a good starting point if the design has an irregular outline. With an opaque JPG, a uniform background is easier to remove than a busy one.

For a first print, pick broad shapes and readable lettering. Shadows and gradients turn into solid color regions. Fine outlines can disappear at the final size when they’re narrower than your printer can lay down.

2. Set the size and build the coaster

Upload your image in the Coaster Maker. In Make it yours, choose color or monochrome, set the finished width, and adjust the maximum color count if needed. Use Build coaster and compare the trace with the original before exporting.

If two details merge, increase the maximum color count and rebuild. If the trace has specks or ragged edges, try a smoother detail setting or simplify the artwork.

3. Choose 3MF or free STL parts

Use Download 3MF to keep the base and artwork parts together with color assignments. 3MF downloads require an account. CoasterPrint shows the credit cost before you confirm. Pro includes unlimited 3MF downloads.

For free STL export, download the parts ZIP. Extract it and import the base and color STLs together as one object with multiple parts. Assign filament colors manually and keep the parts aligned.

4. Inspect the slice in Bambu Studio

  1. Open the 3MF and check that the printer profile, nozzle, and filament assignments match your setup.
  2. For a smoother artwork surface, rotate the entire assembled coaster so the artwork faces down on the build plate. Keep the base and color parts together.
  3. Slice and inspect the first layers. Check that the colored surfaces contact the plate as intended and that thin lettering or outlines still appear. If an area starts above the build plate or the preview suggests supports, inspect the geometry and orientation before printing.
